To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T‐2 contaminated corn flour samples were detected in the Turkish market and the HPLC method is suitable to detect the T‐2 in the grain and grain products.
the T‐2 was detected using the HPLC with UV detector at the wavelength 208 nm, and the identify of toxin was further confirmed by the TLC.
the T‐2 toxins were detected in two corn flour samples at a level of (1.60 and 4.0 ppm).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of T‐2 in grain and grain product consumed in Turkey.
the determination of T‐2 mycotoxin in corn flour and grain products by high performance liquid chromatographic (HPLC).
the detection of T‐2 in corn flour samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T‐2 contaminated corn flour samples were detected in the market in Turkey.
the consumption of contaminated grain and grain product may cause serious human health problems.
there was no T‐2 toxin found in any other samples except the two corn flour samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T‐2 contaminated samples were found to be in the market, and the consumption of these samples could cause serious health problems.
T‐2 toxin is not a common contaminant of the grain and grain products sold in Turkish markets.
T‐2 toxin can be detected in grain and grain product using HPLC and further identification can be confirmed by TLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T‐2 toxins can be detected and identified in corn flour and other grain and grain products.
the HPLC method is more sensitive than the TLC method in the analysis of T‐2 in the grain samples.
T‐2 toxin contamination in grain and grain product consumed especially by Turkish people is a serious health problem.
